sentences.text: The holotype specimen, which is the single example used to define the species, represents a juvenile individual that stood roughly half a meter high at the hip.
Although the full size of an adult is unknown, scientists estimate it could have grown to between three and three and a half meters in length.
Fossils were unearthed by researchers from the University of California Museum of Paleontology within the Navajo Nation in northeastern Arizona.
This single find, cataloged as UCMP V128659, came from the silty layers of the Kayenta Formation.
Kayentavenator shared its world with other dinosaurs including Dilophosaurus, Coelophysis, and the armored Scelidosaurus.
The ecosystem also supported sharks, lungfish, the frog Prosalirus, and the pterosaur Rhamphinion.
Evidence from the ground includes fossilized droppings and footprints left by various reptiles and early mammals.
This creature is classified as a saurischian theropod belonging to the Tetanurae group, with the species name Kayentavenator elysiae.
Analysis suggests it differs from the contemporary Dilophosaurus by having a pubic fenestra and is more closely related to Allosaurus than to Coelophysidae.
The animal lived during the Early Jurassic, specifically between 199 and 182 million years ago, a time spanning the Sinemurian and Pliensbachian stages.
Its environment featured a distinct seasonal pattern with wet summers and arid winters.
Water sources such as streams, ponds, and lakes were plentiful during this period.
Some experts question whether Kayentavenator is a distinct valid taxon or merely a junior synonym of Megapnosaurus kayentakatae.
